usHistory.tagline: reconstruction to right now — the american story is still being argued over.
usHistory.intro: The Civil War ends; the argument over the country does not. We follow that argument from Reconstruction to right now through the people, choices, disasters, breakthroughs, and strange side stories that made the United States what it is. You will change your mind sometimes. Good.

hiddenHistory.tagline: coverups, conspiracies, hoaxes, and the evidence that sorts them out.
hiddenHistory.intro: Some of the wildest government stories are true. Plenty aren't. We open the files, check where every claim came from, and learn when the honest answer is 'we don't know.' Watergate, MKUltra, COINTELPRO, UFOs, hoaxes—the fun is figuring out which box each one belongs in.

beyondTheScoreboard.tagline: american history through sports. the games were never just games.
beyondTheScoreboard.intro: Sports are never sealed off from the rest of the country. Money, television, law, race, protest, labor, and politics all walk onto the field with the players. We start with the games, then follow whatever they reveal about America. The class ends close to home with a Michigan sports story you choose.

about.title: about
about.intro: the teacher, the idea, and where everything on this site belongs.
about.teacherBodyOne: I'm Mr. Auch. I teach US History, Hidden History, and Beyond the Scoreboard. My room is relaxed on purpose. We joke around, chase strange questions, argue over what really happened, and somehow cover a ridiculous amount of history along the way.
about.teacherBodyTwo: The goal is not to make school feel more like school. It is to make the story interesting enough that you want to know what happens next. If you leave class laughing and accidentally remember why Reconstruction failed or how television changed sports, that works for me.
about.siteBody: The Desk keeps the slides, games, source packets, class tools, and odd detours in one place. Google Classroom still handles assignments, grades, and turn-ins.
about.contactBody: Students and families can reach me through Google Classroom or my school email.
about.gradesAnswer: No. Grades, assignments, and turn-ins are in Google Classroom.
about.hiddenQuestion: is hidden history a conspiracy-theory class?
about.hiddenAnswer: It is a class about finding out which extraordinary stories are documented, which fall apart, and which remain honestly unproven. Watergate, MKUltra, and COINTELPRO sit beside famous hoaxes for a reason.
